what_happened: Scene L8/S8: single grey basin with a drainboard, faucet with a horizontal spout ending in a round spray head and a small paddle lever at the right side of the column base, directly under the spout arm. Stages 0/1: pan (pan_5, wooden handle) grasped by the handle at 140, lowered flat into the basin and released at 259 (stage 0 at 271). Sponge grasped at 368 and dropped into the pan at 507 (stage 1 at 529). Both lie fully in the basin until the end. Stage 2: the gripper went to the spout head at 600-720, then down to the lever by 754. It stayed in contact with the lever for about 200 steps (754-953) without moving it. At 968-992 it swept the lever sideways to 0.214 rad (water needs > 0.40; range 0-0.5). At about 992 the lever slipped out of the finger gap and the arm left. 1040-1160 it backed off and looked down at the sink (no water). It re-approached the lever twice: 1220-1256 (one-step touch, no change) and 1508-1556. The second visit pushed the lever back from 0.214 to 0.119 rad. At 1560-1600 the arm swung away.
causal_chain: both objects in by 529 (1071 steps left; stage 2 median 232) -> dwell at the lever 754-953 without moving it -> sweep 968-992 reaches 0.214 rad, lever slips out of the fingers -> retreat and two short re-approaches (1220-1256, 1508-1556) that do not push it further (the last one pushes it back to 0.119) -> water never on at 1600
self_recovery: Two re-approaches to the lever (1220-1256, 1508-1556). Neither re-engaged the lever properly; the second moved it back toward off.
official_criterion_notes: The pan and sponge stayed fully inside the basin, and turning the lever did not disturb them. The packet's fixtures.sink.gripper_touch_intervals count contact with any sink geom (spout head included), so 618-706 is the spout head and 754-1013 is the lever.

packet_facts: pan hold 140-259 lift 0.108; sponge hold 368-507; both at target to 1600

uncertain_about: Why the lever slipped at 0.214 rad. The wrist view shows it leaving the finger gap while the hand moved up/sideways. I cannot tell whether the arm was at a reach or orientation limit.
